source_excerpt: Bengaluru The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18) on Friday (October 30, 2026) successfully launched the NVS-03 satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, according to the ISRO. The GSLV-F18 with the NVS-03 satellite lifted off from the second launch pad of the spaceport and, 18 minutes later placed the satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit. “The GSLV-F18 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the NVS-03 satellite weighing 2250 kg in the intended elliptical orbit. Let me congratulate each and every team member of ISRO, industrial partners, academia for this outstanding accomplishment,” ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan said. He added that the vehicle systems have performed as predicted and as expected. According to the ISRO, the satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock, along with procured atomic clocks. “It also includes L1 signal in addition to existing L5/S signals with coverage over India landmass and a region extending 1,500 km around Indian geopolitical boundary,” the ISRO said. With NavIC setback, India unable to use satellite system for security purposes: experts With NavIC setback, India unable to use satellite system for security purposes: experts A major setback occurred after the last atomic clock on board the Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System-1F (IRNSS-1F) stopped functioning on March 10, leaving only three satellites of the NavIC constellation in function; armed forces of countries use the navigation satellite system for logistics, mapping and operational planning, and relying on a foreign navigation satellite system could pose security issues, especially during wars With NavIC setback, India unable to use satellite system for security purposes: experts storyline 1 NavIC is India’s independent regional navigation satellite system designed to provide accurate position, navigation, and Timing (PNT) services to users in India as well as the region extending about 1,500 km beyond the Indian landmass, which is its primary service area. The successful launch of the NVS-03, which will have a mission life of 12 years, is expected to restore the functioning of the NavIC constellation, which has been weakened due to repeated failures of atomic clocks and the ISRO’s inability to place its previous replacement satellite, NVS-02, in its intended orbit. It can be recalled that earlier this year, on March 13, the last functioning atomic clock aboard IRNSS-1F had stopped working. The ISRO Chairman said that with the success of the mission, the NavIC constellation is restored to the minimum operational configuration with four satellites. “Already three satellites are successfully working in orbit, with this satellite we will have four satellites and restore the PNT services of the country. As you know, the NavIC constellation is a strategic national asset that provides the nation independent access to PNT services. It is also used for civilian applications like real-time tracking of trains along with tracking of vehicles and shipping vessels. It is an important component of the One Nation One Time Project,” the ISRO Chairman said. Friday’s (October 30, 2026) launch is only the third mission to be launched by ISRO in 2026, after the PSLV-C62 mission carrying the EOS-N1 Earth observation satellite on January 12, 2026, and the EOS-05 aboard the GSLV-F17 on September 4. While the PSLV-C62 mission was a failure, the GSLV-F17 mission was a success. “This mission was accomplished with the least turnaround time of just 56 days between successive GSLV missions,” Dr. Narayanan said. PM Modi congratulates ISRO Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated ISRO for the successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03. “This mission marks an important step in strengthening NavIC, our indigenous satellite navigation system,” Mr. Modi said in a post on X. The dedication and ingenuity of our space scientists continue to make our nation proud, he added.
hi_body:
भारतीय अंतरिक्ष अनुसंधान संगठन (ISRO) ने 30 अक्टूबर, 2026 को जियोसिंक्रोनस सैटेलाइट लॉन्च व्हीकल (GSLV-F18) का उपयोग करके NVS-03 उपग्रह को सफलतापूर्वक लॉन्च किया। यह प्रक्षेपण श्रीहरिकोटा के सतीश धवन अंतरिक्ष केंद्र से किया गया, और लॉन्च के 18 मिनट बाद उपग्रह को निर्धारित जियोसिंक्रोनस ट्रांसफर ऑर्बिट में स्थापित कर दिया गया।

## मिशन का महत्व
2,250 किलोग्राम वजन वाला NVS-03 उपग्रह, 'नेविगेशन विद इंडियन कॉन्स्टेलेशन' (NavIC) प्रणाली का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है। इस मिशन ने NavIC तारामंडल को न्यूनतम चार उपग्रहों की परिचालन स्थिति में बहाल कर दिया है, जिससे:
*   भारत के लिए विश्वसनीय स्थिति, नेविगेशन और समय (PNT) सेवाएं फिर से बहाल हो सकेंगी।
*   सुरक्षा संबंधी रसद, मैपिंग और परिचालन योजना में मदद मिलेगी।
*   ट्रेन, वाहन और जहाजों की वास्तविक समय में ट्रैकिंग जैसी नागरिक सेवाएं सुचारू होंगी।
*   'वन नेशन वन टाइम' परियोजना को मजबूती मिलेगी।

## तकनीकी विशेषताएं
उपग्रह में सटीक समय के लिए स्वदेशी और खरीदे गए परमाणु घड़ियों का उपयोग किया गया है। यह L1, L5 और S संकेतों के माध्यम से भारतीय भूभाग और उसके चारों ओर 1,500 किमी के क्षेत्र में कवरेज प्रदान करता है। उपग्रह का मिशन जीवन 12 वर्ष का है।

ISRO अध्यक्ष डॉ. वी. नारायणन ने पुष्टि की कि मिशन पूरी तरह से सफल रहा है और वाहन प्रणालियों ने उम्मीद के अनुसार काम किया है। प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने इस उपलब्धि पर ISRO को बधाई देते हुए कहा कि यह मिशन भारत की स्वदेशी नेविगेशन प्रणाली को मजबूत करने की दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण कदम है। मिशन से जुड़ी विस्तृत जानकारी ISRO की आधिकारिक वेबसाइट पर देखी जा सकती है।

en_body:
On October 30, 2026, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) successfully launched the NVS-03 satellite using the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18). The liftoff occurred at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, with the satellite reaching its intended geosynchronous transfer orbit 18 minutes after launch.

## Mission Objectives and Significance
The NVS-03 satellite, weighing 2,250 kg, is a crucial addition to the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC) system. By restoring the constellation to a minimum operational configuration of four satellites, this mission aims to:
*   Restore reliable Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) services for India.
*   Support security-related logistics, mapping, and operational planning.
*   Enable civilian applications, including real-time tracking of trains, vehicles, and shipping vessels.
*   Contribute to the 'One Nation One Time' project.

## Technical Details
The satellite is equipped with both indigenous and procured atomic clocks to ensure precision. It transmits L1, L5, and S signals, providing coverage across the Indian landmass and a 1,500 km buffer zone. The satellite has an expected mission life of 12 years.

ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan confirmed that the vehicle systems performed as predicted, noting that this launch was achieved with a 56-day turnaround time between GSLV missions. Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised the accomplishment, describing the mission as a vital step in reinforcing India’s indigenous navigation capabilities. Further details and updates regarding the satellite's performance can be verified via the official ISRO website and social media channels.
en_title: ISRO Successfully Launches NVS-03 Navigation Satellite via GSLV-F18
